implementation_notes: Scala has no atomics of its own; on the JVM it uses java.util.concurrent.atomic and VarHandle, which the Scala 3 standard library surfaces as Atomic types. The idiomatic Scala answer for most concurrency is either an immutable structure with an AtomicReference swap (the copy-on-write snapshot, which gives lock-free reads) or a java.util.concurrent structure such as ConcurrentHashMap or LongAdder for contended counters - LongAdder is the striped counter that avoids the cache-line ping-pong of a single AtomicLong. Scala's case classes make the immutable snapshot cheap to write and the swap to publish it is a single atomic reference store.
idiom_name: java.util.concurrent.atomic + AtomicReference snapshot swap; LongAdder for contended counters
pitfalls: @tailrec on a CAS retry loop is required for the recursion to be optimised; without it a long retry chain grows the stack.
A mutable case class inside the AtomicReference defeats the whole approach - the value must be immutable for a lost CAS to be safely retryable.
AtomicLong is a single contended counter and will ping-pong its cache line; LongAdder is striped and is the right choice under real contention.
Scala's standard library atomics are JVM types, so this is not a portable answer - Scala.js and Scala Native need a different story.
